gaps.sentence: ___ of the two films has been shown on television.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two films has ...' is correct for two items; 'none' is not used for two and 'both/all' need a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: There's ___ of room for improvement in this essay.
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of room' is the fixed pattern; 'a lot of' would need the article 'a', which is not in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: I looked everywhere, but I couldn't find my keys ___.
gaps.explanation: After a negative verb, 'anywhere' is used; 'somewhere' belongs to affirmative sentences.

gaps.sentence: I put ___ sugar in your tea by mistake.
gaps.explanation: 'Too much' is used before uncountable nouns like sugar; 'too sugar' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: He had ___ money, so he couldn't even buy a bus ticket.
gaps.explanation: 'Had no money' states zero and explains the result; 'none' cannot stand directly before a noun.

gaps.sentence: ___ of her two brothers lives abroad.
gaps.explanation: 'Each of her two brothers lives ...' is correct; 'every' cannot take 'of' and 'both/all' need a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: ___ of my two brothers work in banking.
gaps.explanation: 'Both of my two brothers work ...' is correct; 'all' and 'none' are not used for two.

gaps.hint: general statement without 'the' — 'people' has no article
gaps.explanation: 'Most people' means people in general; 'most of' needs 'the' (most of the people).
